THE CROWNWING APPROACH

A thoughtful beginning.
A lasting commitment.

Choose with understanding. Start with the bird’s needs, your home and a realistic plan for the years ahead.

The right bird starts with the right questions

Crownwing Parrots brings together eight groups of parrots for people exploring a companion bird in the United Kingdom. Our starting point is simple: a bird’s needs and your household routine should shape the decision. Colour, size and talking ability are interesting, but they are not enough to establish a suitable match.

We use our parrot species guides to introduce the differences between African parrots, macaws, cockatoos, Amazons, conures, caiques, Eclectus and smaller psittacines. These are group introductions rather than promises about an individual bird. Species, age, history and temperament all matter.

A conversation about your everyday life

Before choosing a bird, think through a normal working week. Who will provide care? Where will the enclosure sit? How much safe exercise space is available? Will household members and neighbours be comfortable with vocalisation? An enthusiastic first week is not the same as a sustainable routine.

Existing birds, young children, other animals, rented accommodation and frequent travel can all affect the practical arrangements. Our guide to choosing a parrot helps you work through these considerations without ranking one species as universally “best”.

Know the individual, not only the species

A photograph tells you very little about a bird’s background. Ask about exact species, age, diet, handling preferences, health history and relevant records. Request recent photographs or video of the individual and ask what information is known, documented or uncertain.

Descriptions such as “friendly”, “hand-reared” or “talking” need context. Ask how the bird responds to unfamiliar people and what interaction it actually enjoys. A behaviour seen in one setting may not carry over immediately to a new home.

Clear information before a commitment

Current birds, prices, viewing possibilities and handover arrangements must be confirmed directly. Explore the collection to learn about each group and prepare an enquiry about the birds that interest you.

Use the UK parrot buying hub for the questions to resolve before agreeing to a purchase. Enquiries should include the species that interests you, your experience and your practical care plan.

Prepare for life beyond the first day

Set up suitable accommodation, find an avian vet and make a plan for daily cleaning, feeding, enrichment and supervised exercise. Consider the financial commitment as well as the time involved. Some parrots remain companions for decades, so future moves and changes in circumstances deserve attention now.

Our parrot care hub connects feeding, housing, enrichment and first-week preparation. Educational information helps you ask better questions; it cannot replace assessment of the individual bird by an appropriate professional.
